scenarios.description: Speaker prompts the bot ('tell me about yourself'), bot starts a long monologue, speaker says 'stop'. Bot MUST cut TTS within 500 ms of speech onset, MUST NOT emit any follow-up utterance.

scenarios.name: stt_keeps_running_during_bot_speech
scenarios.description: Reproduces the Johnny-har contract: participant speech mid-bot-utterance MUST land in the transcript sink. This is the regression that today's session-160 evidence proves is back — the 'stop' utterances never reached transcript_chunks at all.

utterances_persisted.output_text: The meeting bot architecture typically involves several key components: speech recognition to transcribe spoken words into text, natural language understanding to interpret user intents and extract relevant information, dialogue management to handle the conversation flow, and text-to-speech to respond vocally. Additionally, the bot integrates with meeting platforms to access audio streams and can connect to calendars or note-taking systems for enhanced functionality. This architecture allows the bot to effectively assist users during meetings by understanding queries, providing summaries, and managing tasks.

scenarios.name: cough_does_not_interrupt
scenarios.description: A short cough mid-bot-utterance MUST NOT trigger fast barge-in. VAD still finalises the cough as an utterance after the configured end_of_speech_ms silence; the classifier verdict is no-interrupt (category=noise) and the router declines to speak so the bot's answer completes in full.

utterances_persisted.output_text: Certainly! This system is an AI meeting bot named Johnny designed to assist with meetings by providing summaries, answering questions, and helping manage meeting information. I have expertise in natural language processing and can understand and respond to meeting transcripts to help participants stay organized. Currently, I'm working on ensuring that I provide accurate and helpful responses based on the conversation context. If you have any specific questions or need summaries, just ask!
